label: early h input (weak), plus diffuse context-dependent firing
explanation: The only reliable regularity is input h at the start of the sequence: h at t=0 is active 100% of the time, but only weakly (~0.02 of max), and h at t<=1 gives precision 0.67, though only 13% of activation mass. Most of the mass is spread across contexts that are individually low-precision: h anywhere in the original phase (36% of mass, 28% precision), digits 1/2 in the original phase (~24% of mass, ~3% rate), and the first copy steps, i.e. the <DEL> step and recall_idx 1 where the first original token is re-input (~30% of mass, 2% rate). The strongest activations (up to max) are at recall_idx 1 for first tokens like h, j, n, 1, k. Activity is concentrated early in each phase (t<=3, and recall_idx 0-2) and nearly absent late in the copy phase (recall_idx>=3). A disjunction of these components reaches 0.80 mass recall but only 5% precision, and none of the simple conditions I tried (position, input token, first token) explained which instances fire. Best F1 is about 0.45.
